sections.h2: Where is Augusta County, Virginia, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Augusta County is in the Shenandoah Valley on the western side of Virginia, and it is one of the largest counties in the state. Its total area is 971 square miles, which Wikipedia lists as second in Virginia by total area and third by land area.

The county completely surrounds the independent cities of Staunton and Waynesboro, and those cities are not part of it. That detail matters for a seller. A house with a Staunton or Waynesboro mailing address may be taxed by the city, while a house just outside the line is taxed by Augusta County.

The county reaches the Blue Ridge, with pieces of the Blue Ridge Parkway, George Washington National Forest and Shenandoah National Park inside its borders. The 2020 census counted 77,487 residents.

sections.h2: Which communities make up Augusta County?
sections.html:
Most residents live in unincorporated communities. The 2010 census figures listed on Wikipedia show Stuarts Draft as the largest at 9,235, followed by Fishersville at 7,462 and Verona at 4,239. Weyers Cave, Crimora and Churchville are smaller.

Two towns sit inside the county. Craigsville had 923 residents in 2010. Grottoes is mostly in Rockingham County, and only seven of its residents live on the Augusta side.

For a seller, the community name on a mailing label does not tell you who bills the tax. The parcel's location does, so use the county's online assessment records or call the offices before assuming.

The county was formed in 1738 from Orange County and named for Princess Augusta of Saxe-Gotha. County government was organized in 1745 and the present boundaries were reached in 1790.

During the Civil War the area was an important agricultural center, and the Battle of Piedmont was fought here on June 5, 1864.

sections.h2: Who are the major employers in Augusta County?
sections.html:
According to the county's 2023 financial report, four employers each have more than 1,000 workers: Augusta County Public Schools, Augusta Medical Center, Hershey and McKee Foods.

  • Employers with 500 to 999 employees include Target, AAF-McQuay, Hollister Co. and the County of Augusta itself.
  • Hospital, school and food manufacturing jobs make up much of the large-employer list.

A seller whose job or a relative's care moves them out of the area can sell without waiting on a long financing process. We buy houses as they are.

sections.h2: When are Augusta County real estate taxes due?
sections.html:
Taxes are due in equal installments on June 5 and December 5. If a date falls on a weekend, the due date moves to the following Monday, and you may pay the full annual amount in June.

In 2024 the county extended the first-half date to June 21. The county's real estate page also says the 2024 rate is $0.52 per $100 of assessed value, set by the Board of Supervisors, and that real estate is assessed as of January 1 by the Real Estate Assessor's Office. Bills can be viewed and paid on the county's e-Treasurer site. We did not confirm the current year's rate, so check your bill.

sections.h2: What are the penalty and interest for late tax in Augusta County?
sections.html:
The county states a 10 percent late payment penalty on the unpaid balance, plus interest at 10 percent a year on what remains unpaid. The state's share of personal property tax is excluded from the interest.

The county also tells taxpayers that they are responsible for knowing due dates. If no bill arrives, contact the taxing office before the due date to arrange payment.

Some reasons never waive the charge. These include not knowing the due date, not getting a bill, a bill mailed to the wrong address, an incorrect bill and wrong information from county staff. The charge may be waived in narrower cases.

  • A medically determinable physical or mental impairment on the due date, with payment within 30 days.
  • The Commissioner of Revenue abates the tax or certifies a clerical error by that office.
  • The late payment was caused solely by the Treasurer or the Commissioner of Revenue.

A taxpayer who cannot pay in full may arrange a payment plan with the Treasurer's Office at (540) 245-5660 or treasurer@co.augusta.va.us. The plan does not remove the penalty and interest keeps running.

sections.h2: How did the 2024 reassessment change values in Augusta County?
sections.html:
The county reassesses on a five-year cycle, and the 2024 reassessment began in September 2022 with notices mailed in February 2024. The county hired Wampler-Eanes Appraisal Group and divided the county into about 96 neighborhoods.

Its published analysis of 2023 residential sales found 680 sales with a median increase of 58.3 percent over the old assessment and an average of 60.9 percent. The highest median increases were in Beverly Manor at 69.5 percent and North River at 68.8 percent. The lowest were in Craigsville at 33.7 percent, based on only three sales, and Wayne at 50.9 percent.

The county's document also explains why it reassesses: the state's sales ratio study flags a locality whose assessments fall below 70 percent of fair market value in a general reassessment year. Augusta's ratios were 89.75 percent in 2019, 83.73 percent in 2020 and 71.7 percent in 2021. Fieldwork included visits to accessible properties to verify records and update property cards and photos.

That context helps a seller. Many owners saw their assessed value rise sharply in 2024, and your new value is a county estimate, not a sale price.

sections.h2: How do you appeal an Augusta County assessment?
sections.html:
The county's reassessment materials describe three steps: an informal hearing with the assessor, the Board of Equalization, then Circuit Court. Informal appeals could be made by Zoom, phone, email, mail or in person.

  • Common reasons given: value that seems too high or too low, market value disparities, changes in condition, comparable sales and clerical errors.
  • The county material did not list deadlines, so use the dates on your notice.

Under Virginia Code section 58.1-3381 the board can increase, decrease or affirm an assessment, and an owner must be notified before an increase. In court, section 58.1-3984 treats the assessor's value as correct and puts the burden on the owner to rebut it by a preponderance of the evidence.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid tax when you sell in Augusta County?
sections.html:
The unpaid tax stays with the property. Virginia Code section 58.1-3340 gives real estate a tax lien that ranks ahead of other liens until paid, and sale proceeds are applied to the tax. How the current year's tax is split between buyer and seller is set by the contract.

On the deed, the grantor tax under section 58.1-802 is 50 cents for each $500 and is paid by the seller unless the parties agree otherwise. The state recordation tax under section 58.1-801 is 25 cents per $100.

State law sets the outer limits on late charges. Section 58.1-3916 caps a locality's penalty at 10 percent of the tax past due or $10, whichever is greater, and interest at 10 percent a year, which matches the figures Augusta County publishes. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure before closing, and keep the receipt for your title company. We buy as is, so an open balance is something we can work through with you.

faqs.q: Are Staunton and Waynesboro part of Augusta County?
faqs.a: No. They are independent cities that Augusta County surrounds. A house inside either city is generally handled by the city, so check which office bills you.

faqs.q: When are Augusta County property taxes due?
faqs.a: June 5 and December 5. A due date on a weekend moves to the following Monday.

faqs.q: What is the late penalty in Augusta County?
faqs.a: The county states a 10 percent penalty on the unpaid balance and 10 percent annual interest. A payment plan does not remove either charge.

faqs.q: Who do I contact about a payment plan?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's Office at (540) 245-5660 or treasurer@co.augusta.va.us.

faqs.q: How many years between Augusta County reassessments?
faqs.a: The county described a five-year cycle, with the latest reassessment taking effect in 2024.
